chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi narrated to me, saying: Musa ibn 'Imran al-Nakha'i narrated to me, saying: al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Sinan from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar
He said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): It is narrated from al-Mughirah that he said: When a man knows his Lord, there is nothing else required of him after that.

He (peace be upon him) said: For him? May God curse him! Is it not that the more one gains knowledge of God, the more obedient he is to Him? So those who do not know Him obey God (Exalted and Mighty).

Indeed, God (Exalted and Mighty) commanded Muhammad (peace be upon him) with a command, and Muhammad (peace be upon him) commanded the believers with a command, so they act upon it until his prohibition comes. And the command and the prohibition are equal in the view of the believer.
Then he said: God (Exalted and Mighty) does not look at a servant and does not purify him [if] he leaves an obligation from the obligations of God and commits a major sin from the major sins.
He said: I said: God does not look at him. He said: Yes.

Indeed, God (Exalted and Mighty) commanded with a command, and Iblis commanded with a command, so he left what God (Exalted and Mighty) commanded and turned to what Iblis commanded. So this one is with Iblis in the seventh depth of Hell.
ai.seo_question: Does knowing God exempt a person from performing obligatory acts and avoiding sins?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) refutes the Gnostic notion that *ma'rifah* (knowledge of God) alone suffices, arguing instead that true knowledge necessitates increased obedience to obedience to divine commands. He illustrates the severity of neglecting a *fard* to follow a specific command—even if from a source like Iblis—by noting that Iblis himself was cast into the lowest depths of Hell for obeying his own command over God's, a fate shared by those who do the same.

One who leaves the order of Allah
and obeys the order of Shaitaan,
